Three subsequent attempts to add a third feature (`extend_best`, `swap_worst`, `refine`) all failed to beat the two-feature rule, triggering my `last_gain_at_most` rule (which I loosened once, with a logged reason, since the anchor itself still looked sound) and eventually my `failures_at_least 3` rule, which I honored by stopping rather than continuing to search for marginal gains.

**Candidate submitted:** Rule **[feature 32 long, feature 35 short]**, in-sample Sharpe 0.483 (all-years equal) / 0.546 (recent-years weighted) — clearly ahead of the baseline model.

**Prediction for unseen data:** Mean net Sharpe **0.28**, SD **0.22**. This haircuts the in-sample figure substantially to account for selection effects from scanning 40 candidates (even though the search itself was short and disciplined, with failed extensions correctly rejected rather than kept), while still expecting the rule to outperform the baseline model out-of-sample.
